title: Departments
markdown:
**What it is:** The org units the Executive works through. Each department has a mission, goals, an authority level, a head, and a specialist agent behind it.

**What it does:**

- Lists every department as a card with its authority (**Auto**, **Propose** or **Escalate**), the start of its mission, its goal count, and a status pill (on track / at risk / off track).
- Creates departments and gives them a mission, goals, budget, and headcount.
- Sets the **authority level**: act on its own, propose for approval, or always escalate.
- Sets a department head and team channels (Slack, Discord, Telegram).
- Runs a recurring check-in where the specialist reviews the department's goals.

**How to use:**

1. Open **Company** in the sidebar, pick the **Departments** tab, and click **Add department**. Enter a **Name** (and, optionally, a **Mission**) and click **Create**. New departments start at *Proposes, you approve* and check in weekly.
2. Open the department. The page shows its specialist, how it acts, its mission, head, headcount, budget, channels, watched entities, its check-in schedule with when the next one is due, and its **In scope** / **Out of scope** lists when it has them. It refreshes every 30 seconds.
3. Click **Edit settings**. The **Department settings** panel opens with five tabs:
   - **Charter**: the **Mission**.
   - **How it acts**: the **Department head** (a team member; the Executive treats them as the department's owner in routing), the authority level (**Acts on its own**, **Proposes, you approve** or **Escalates to a person**), and the **Recurring check-in**: **Daily** (pick a time), **Weekly** (pick a day and a time) or **Off**. Times are UTC. New departments check in on Monday at 09:00. A change takes effect straight away.
   - **Numbers**: **Headcount** and **Budget (USD)**.
   - **Channels**: a **Slack channel**, **Discord channel** and **Telegram group**, picked by name. When set, the Executive posts department updates there. Left blank, messages go to the department head by DM. Slack and Discord suggest the channel named most like the department (**Closest match**); it is saved only when you click **Save settings**, and **Pick another** or **Clear** drops it. **Telegram group** lists groups the bot is in and has seen a message from. Not listed? Add the bot to the group and send any message there. **Enter an ID by hand** takes a raw ID instead. Only the principal sees these lists; anyone else enters IDs by hand.
   - **Watched**: **Watched entities (one per line)**, such as vendors, competitors or tickers. The Executive starts watching their status pages, filings and feeds on its own and sends what it finds to this department and its head.

   Then click **Save settings**, or **Cancel** to drop the changes.
4. Click **Add goal**. Type **What's the goal?** (the only required field), pick a timeframe chip (**This week**, **This month**, **This quarter**, **This year** or **Ongoing**; the default is this quarter), optionally fill in **Target** and **Where it stands now**, and click **Add goal**. A new goal starts on track until a check-in grades it.
5. Each goal shows its status, timeframe, target, where it stands now, and when it was last reviewed (marked if that was more than 10 days ago). Its **⋯** menu has **Edit goal** (change the goal, timeframe, status, target and where it stands now, then **Save**) and **Delete goal**.
6. **Delete department**, in the **⋯** menu next to **Edit settings**, removes the department. Its goals stay on the **Goals** page with no department, each on its owner (a goal nobody owned goes to the department's head). It can't be undone.

**What the authority level covers:** the department's check-ins, scheduled messages and alerts, and what its team members ask for in chat. Operations also covers meetings people ask for. It doesn't cover what the Executive does on its own under Take the lead; **Always asks first** there holds that.

**From chat:**

- Tell the Executive what happened and it updates the matching goal's status and progress, and records why.
- Tell it a new target and it adds the goal. A goal doesn't need a department: it goes under one only when you name it (a new name creates it), and it's yours unless you name a teammate to own it. Only the principal can do this, from the web app or their own Slack or Discord. A teammate or an email can't. It adds one goal for each target you actually give it: at most 5 in one message and at most 8 per department (or 8 with no department) this way. Ask it to "set up some goals" and it asks you which ones.
- Ask it to make someone the head of a department.

**Examples from chat:** *"We closed 40% of the Q3 ARR target."* · *"We lost the Acme deal."* · *"New Sales goal: 20 paying customers by December 31."* · *"Make Sarah the head of Marketing."*

**Goals page:** the **Goals** tab of **Company** (of **You** when you use Open Executive just for yourself) lists every goal in one place. Every goal has an owner; a department is optional. **Group by** shows them by **Owner** (you first), **Department** (once you have one; **Area** when it's just you) or **Status**. The top line counts the goals and how many are off track, at risk and on track. Each goal has **Edit goal** and **Delete goal** in its **⋯** menu; editing also changes its **Owner** and **Department**. Click **Add goal**, type the goal, and optionally pick its **Owner** (you by default) and **Department** (**None** by default, or **New department…** to create one), then fill it in as above. With no goals yet, the page opens on **Add your first goal**. Every goal is checked weekly: a department with a specialist checks its own goals, and the Executive reviews the rest every Monday, so a goal slipping shows up in your brief either way.

**Departments tab:** it appears once you have a department. Until then, the Goals page has an **Add a department** link for when you want a lead, its own authority and its own check-in for part of the company.

**Who can change it:** anyone signed in can add, edit and delete departments and goals on these pages.

**Just for yourself?** In that mode department check-ins are paused (the department page says so; the weekly goal review still checks every goal) and **Company** becomes **You**, with **Goals** and no **Departments** tab. The departments are still there. Open `/departments` to change an area's settings. A department can't be renamed on these pages.

*Note: the authority level is what decides whether the Executive acts on its own or asks first within that department's scope.*
